paragraphs: Back in July, Apple updated its TestFlight app with a basic search feature. While you might think this simple update would be universally welcomed, the same TestFlight app introduced a pretty frustrating bug for a lot of users.
Personally, I wasn’t affected by the bug in a way that I noticed. For this reason, I thought the TestFlight update was a simple but significant step forward.
Sometimes a small change can make a big impact. That’s especially true for Apple’s latest TestFlight update for users with a lot of pre-release software.
Apple just updated TestFlight for iPhone, iPad, Mac, and more. The new version, 4.3, introduces “a search field to quickly find apps.”
In retrospect, I did notice something odd that I flagged at the end of the post (but got backwards in my assessment):
The update also surfaced more apps in the “previously tested” category, so maybe the usual bug fix and performance improvements may relate to that.

I missed that this was actually the bug, I think, because I left several years of app TestFlights to “merge” my separate iCloud and App Store Apple accounts last year. Inconvenient requirement, but worth it for me.
